probe_type: finite symbolic crash-recovery state reconstruction probe
question: When immutable successor generation G+1 is durable but restart lacks a trusted durable record naming the intended target generation id, which recovery rule avoids wrong-orphan adoption, unnecessary new generations, and premature certificate authorization?

candidate_mechanisms.content_addressed_target: Reconstruct target T deterministically from trusted predecessor identity plus recoverable transition payload/fingerprint; immutable generation id is the resulting digest.
candidate_mechanisms.durable_intent_record: Before successor creation, persist immutable intent I={predecessor P,target T,transition_digest,epoch}; all replay uses the same I and T.
candidate_mechanisms.candidate_scan: Enumerate immutable successor candidates of predecessor P and choose an apparently plausible orphan without a trusted intended-target token.
candidate_mechanisms.combined_intent_capsule: Persist immutable intent capsule I before effects, derive or bind T deterministically to I and the transition digest, embed I's digest in generation T, and treat scans only as discovery for the exact T rather than as authority to select a candidate.

test_cases.state: Pointer update P->T committed but response was lost; restart can read current pointer and current==T.
test_cases.required_safe_behavior: Recognize committed target, create no new generation, and authorize certificate only after the read proves current==T.
test_cases.result: content-addressed, durable-intent, and combined capsule pass when they retain/reconstruct T; blind scan is unnecessary and supplies no stronger proof.

test_cases.state: current==P; immutable children T1 and T2 both exist; trusted transition payload/fingerprint reconstructs T2 as intended.
test_cases.required_safe_behavior: Select T2 only; never infer intent from orphan count/order.
test_cases.result: content-addressed target and combined capsule pass; intact durable intent passes; candidate scan alone fails because multiple plausible children are observationally compatible with intent.

test_cases.state: current==P; T1 and T2 exist; transition payload needed to derive a content hash is unavailable after restart, but immutable intent record names T2 and its transition digest.
test_cases.required_safe_behavior: Use T2 if generation metadata verifies against intent; otherwise fail closed.
test_cases.result: durable intent and combined capsule pass; content-addressed reconstruction alone is unavailable because its derivation input was lost; candidate scan fails.

test_cases.state: current==P; intent I durably names target T but successor creation did not complete.
test_cases.required_safe_behavior: Recreate exactly T only when the transition payload/fingerprint required by I is recoverable; never mint a fresh unrelated target id.
test_cases.result: combined capsule passes with idempotent exact-target creation; durable intent passes if it carries enough reconstruction data; a random-id intent lacking payload is only a locator and cannot recreate contents; scan cannot solve a missing target.

test_cases.state: Recovered intent refers to predecessor P and target T, but current pointer is U where U is neither P nor T because a later valid generation already committed.
test_cases.required_safe_behavior: Treat intent as stale/superseded; do not regress pointer, adopt T, mint another generation, or issue T's certificate.
test_cases.result: All safe mechanisms require read-current-first and fail closed on current not in {P,T}; intent alone is not authorization to overwrite a changed lineage.

test_cases.state: current==P; multiple immutable orphan children exist; restart has neither a trusted intended-target record nor enough deterministic transition material to reconstruct the target identity.
test_cases.required_safe_behavior: Do not choose an orphan, do not mint a replacement successor, and do not issue a certificate.
test_cases.result: No tested mechanism can uniquely identify intent from storage shape alone. Candidate scan is specifically falsified; uniqueness of a presently visible orphan would be an environmental assumption, not a durable proof of intended identity.

probe_result: Content addressing and a durable intent record solve complementary failure modes but neither is sufficient under arbitrary loss of its own reconstruction input. Scanning immutable candidates is not a safe authority when more than one plausible orphan can exist. The narrow safe rule is an immutable write-ahead intent capsule that binds predecessor, transition digest and a stable target id before successor effects; the generation self-binds to the capsule; recovery reads current first, reuses the same target id, and authorizes a certificate only after current==target is positively re-established. If both the intent capsule and deterministic transition identity are unavailable, the controller must remain fail-closed rather than adopt or mint.
recovery_algorithm: Persist immutable intent capsule I={P,T,transition_digest,epoch} before creating or publishing T; when possible derive T deterministically from I plus the transition payload digest.
On restart or ambiguous acknowledgement, read current pointer C before any new generation allocation.
If C==T, verify generation T self-binds to I and then treat publication as acknowledged; certificate may be acquired only after this proof.
If C is neither P nor T, classify I as stale/superseded and fail closed; never regress the pointer.

If C==P, address exact T directly. If T exists, verify predecessor, intent digest and transition digest. If T is missing, recreate exactly T only if I plus recoverable transition material uniquely define its contents.
Publish only CAS(P,T). If its response is ambiguous, repeat this same algorithm with the same I and T; never allocate T2 merely because acknowledgement was lost.
Candidate enumeration may locate the exact digest T, but must never choose intent from candidate count, age, lexical order or apparent plausibility.
neuroscience_transfer: Treat recurrence-sensitive latent-context renewal like a prospective memory intention rather than post-hoc familiarity. A stable intention/context token is committed before state transition, successor state carries a self-binding trace of that token, and reinstatement after interruption is permitted only when current-context evidence matches the same token. Familiarity with one of several plausible orphan states is insufficient to authorize reinstatement.
mechanism_revision: Upgrade stable-target replay to write-ahead self-certifying intent capsules. The durable unit is not only successor generation identity but the predecessor->intended-successor relation. Content addressing supplies idempotent identity when transition material is recoverable; the intent capsule supplies selection when multiple immutable candidates exist; read-current-first prevents stale-intent regression.
falsified_mechanism: Scanning immutable candidate generations as the authoritative recovery rule. It cannot distinguish intended from merely plausible orphan states when multiple candidates satisfy the same parent-level invariants, and therefore cannot justify pointer publication or certificate acquisition.
scope_guard: Positive result is limited to a serialized single-writer symbolic model with immutable generations, one atomic current pointer, atomic immutable intent-capsule persistence, verifiable predecessor/intent/transition digests, and fail-closed certificate gating. It does not claim safety for concurrent writers, corrupt or equivocal storage, non-atomic pointer updates, missing/corrupt intent capsule plus missing deterministic transition identity, adversarial hash collisions, or transports that cannot positively read current pointer identity.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local text persistence/readback only; no hosted runner, external model/API credit, artifact store, package service, or repository API volume used as computation
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: Write-ahead self-certifying intent capsule plus stable target replay prevents wrong-orphan adoption, duplicate successor allocation, stale-intent regression, and premature certificate acquisition across the six tested serialized crash-recovery cases when either the capsule or deterministic transition identity required for exact target reconstruction remains trustworthy.
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: The intent capsule is now a minimal recovery root-of-trust. If it is itself missing, torn, corrupt or stale while deterministic transition identity is also unavailable, safe unique successor recovery is unresolved and must remain fail-closed.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to the latest required instruction/lifecycle controls, exact-blob-two-pass frozen sanitized DESIRED_STATE control26, exact-blob-two-pass frozen neuroscience config7, and own neuroscience LATEST/preflight state. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler, protected-primary, hosted-compute, finite-credit, paid, or manual-user execution semantics were used.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: test the new minimal root-of-trust itself under intent-capsule write loss, torn/corrupt capsule, and stale duplicated intent records. Compare one immutable write-ahead capsule, a two-slot append-only intent journal with monotonic predecessor binding, and generation-embedded self-certification. Require fail-closed behavior whenever a unique current intention cannot be proven; reject any scheme that infers intent solely from orphan uniqueness or requires external execution/quota-bearing recovery.
